source.title: Results from the Turing Seminar hackathon

record.file_problem: The post is present in full, but it only summarizes a student project and does not include the project report or its methods.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports a vision-CNN comparison of neuron and dictionary-feature monosemanticity, a different measurement aimed at the claim about whether neurons have coherent meanings.
record.gate_note: The post reports the student project's result that 2 of 100 random neurons were found interpretable and monosemantic, compared with 46 of 100 random features. This is a reported project result, not a result from an experiment described in detail in the post. The feature count is a reference comparison, not a separate result about neurons. The counts do not establish that the other neurons respond to several unrelated inputs.
record.test_reason: This is a hackathon round-up post. Its only relevant content is a quoted result from a separate, linked student report. That report adapts dictionary learning to a vision CNN and finds 2 of 100 random neurons interpretable and monosemantic, against 46 of 100 features. The post runs no experiment and gives no methods, model or neuron examples. Even taken at face value, 'not interpretable and monosemantic' does not separate polysemantic neurons from uninterpretable ones. So it does not show neurons responding to several unrelated inputs (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The post author praises the project as 'very good execution' and quotes its neuron-vs-feature counts. He draws no conclusion about polysemanticity. The counts come from the student project, not the post author.
record.recipe_differences: The project adapts dictionary learning for vision CNNs and compares interpretability and monosemanticity of neurons and features; the post does not specify the procedure in enough detail to compare it more closely with the original method.

fits_no_version.finding: The quoted project result: in a vision CNN, dictionary-learning features were judged interpretable and monosemantic far more often than neurons (46/100 vs 2/100).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary features in vision CNNs are more often monosemantic than individual neurons.

record.problems: The post gives only a brief summary: it does not name the CNN, explain how interpretability or monosemanticity was assessed, or report uncertainty. A low count of neurons judged interpretable and monosemantic does not by itself demonstrate unrelated mixed responses.
record.rows_left_out: No additional neuronal results are reported. The 46-of-100 feature count is retained as the reference in R1 rather than recorded as a separate neuron result.

untested.parts: Whether any neuron in the (unnamed) CNN responds to several unrelated inputs. The InceptionV1 example is not examined.

missing.what: The underlying project report 'Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Vision Models with Dictionary Learning' (Heurtel-Depeiges). It likely contains the model, the scoring method and neuron examples bearing on V1/V3. It should be retrieved and assessed as its own study.
missing.locator: Linked Google Drive file in the 'Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Vision Models' section

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' is downgraded because the only result is a secondhand quote of another document. A commenter discusses feature 8's description but gives no neuron result.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not identify the vision model or report which inputs activated neurons, so it does not establish whether any neuron responded to multiple unrelated inputs or address the InceptionV1 example.

rows.subject: vision CNN (model not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Counted random neurons found interpretable and monosemantic in a dictionary-learning project.

conditions.value: adaptation of dictionary learning for vision CNNs

rows.locator: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Vision Models with Dictionary Learning
rows.note: The post calls the project execution very good. The result indicates fewer neurons than features were judged interpretable and monosemantic, but does not show that the other neurons respond to several unrelated inputs.
rows.check: This is a result cited from a separate linked project report, not the post's own result. The CNN is not named and the scoring method is not given. 'Not interpretable and monosemantic' mixes polysemantic with uninterpretable, so it cannot show V1's unrelated-input responses. The 46/100 feature count is the comparison method, not a neuron baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
